title: Silas and the Scholarship
premise: Beatrix Okafor has one shot at the Halloway Scholarship: a semester-long capstone debate project that her teacher insists she complete with Silas Reyes, the boy whose family's testimony once helped evict hers. Forced into partnership, they uncover documents proving the eviction was engineered by the same benefactor who funds Beatrix's scholarship — meaning exposing the truth could destroy her future, and defending the lie would betray Silas, who is quietly losing his home to the same scheme. As their reluctant alliance deepens into something neither will name, Beatrix must choose between the scholarship she's counted on for survival and the truth that could save them both. In the end she tells the whole story before the selection committee, forfeiting the award — and discovers the committee's youngest member, moved by her honesty, opens a door to a different kind of future.
about_author: Edmund Lockridge is a former high school debate coach who spent eleven years watching teenagers argue beautifully about everything except what mattered to them. He writes from a small town in Ohio, where he still judges tournaments and keeps every losing ballot.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix counts down to graduation in her journal, mapping escape routes out of a house where her parents' arguments drown out her victories. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: restless claustrophobia and fierce hope.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Ms. Whitfield announces the capstone project and reads partners aloud: Okafor and Reyes. The class goes silent; Silas doesn't look up. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: public humiliation sharpened into private dread.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Seated
chapters.summary: Silas arrives at the library first, having already outlined three topics. His competence infuriates her more than his silence. They agree on nothing except a truce until Friday. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grudging recognition of an equal.

chapters.title: What Silas Carries
chapters.summary: Silas's POV reveals his father's failing job at Delacroix Development and the final notice taped to the fridge — the same company named in Beatrix's old eviction papers. He says nothing. Emotional beat: shame and protective secrecy.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: They draft a partnership contract as a joke that isn't one: no personal questions, no past grievances, no lying about sources. Beatrix signs fast. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: brittle humor over old wounds.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Researching housing policy, Beatrix finds a 2011 city council record: Delacroix's lawyer coached witnesses against her family. Her hands shake; Silas watches her read it. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the past arriving like a slap.

chapters.title: Denial, Structured
chapters.summary: Silas argues the document proves nothing — lawyers do their jobs. Their first real fight ends with him walking out, but he copies the file before he goes. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loyalty to family colliding with doubt.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Okafors'
chapters.summary: A group-project dinner forces the families together. Beatrix's mother recognizes Silas's surname and goes cold; Silas sees, for the first time, the faces behind the case files. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: uncomfortable empathy taking root.

chapters.title: The Benefactor
chapters.summary: Beatrix traces the Halloway Scholarship's funding to a Delacroix family trust. Exposing the eviction means indicting the hand that feeds her. She tells no one. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: vertigo — survival and integrity pulling apart.

chapters.title: Practice Round
chapters.summary: Whitfield runs mock debates; Beatrix and Silas are electric together, finishing each other's arguments. Afterwards, alone, the electricity doesn't stop. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the first almost-moment, interrupted by his phone buzzing with another notice.

chapters.title: Silas Breaks a Rule
chapters.summary: He breaks rule one and asks about her father. She breaks rule three and admits she's terrified of losing the scholarship. Something unguarded opens between them. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: intimacy through confession.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Someone photographs their archive findings and sends them to the school board. Rumors fly that Beatrix is attacking her own benefactor. Silas suspects his father's employer is watching. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening around them both.

chapters.title: Choose a Side
chapters.summary: Beatrix's parents demand she drop the topic; Silas's father begs him to protect the family name. Both are ordered to betray each other. Neither does. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love against duty, declared silently.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Records Office
chapters.summary: They break into the county annex after hours for the original deed filings and find proof of a coordinated campaign of evictions. A security guard nearly catches them; Silas covers for her. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.summary: Silas's family receives an expedited eviction date — retaliation, they suspect. He withdraws from the project to shield Beatrix, telling her it's what he wants. She knows he's lying. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Beatrix works alone and hates it. Whitfield warns her the committee is watching the controversy — the scholarship may already be gone. She realizes she stopped caring which is the greater loss. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: clarity arriving through grief.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Delacroix
chapters.summary: Beatrix confronts the trust's representative, who offers her a quiet deal: drop the story, keep the money, help Silas's family stay. Everything she wants, priced at the truth. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: For the first time, Beatrix wins the argument at home — not by debating, but by showing her parents the deed and saying she'd rather lose with them than win without. Her mother hands her the old case file. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: reconciliation and inheritance of courage.

chapters.title: Silas Comes Back
chapters.summary: Silas returns with his father's blessing and a box of Delacroix's internal memos his mother kept from her years in their office. Together they build the full case overnight. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt, love finally spoken plainly.

chapters.title: Before the Committee
chapters.summary: The capstone presentation becomes a public reckoning: the evictions, the trust, the offer made to her. Beatrix tells all of it, then formally withdraws from scholarship consideration. The room is silent. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the climax — truth chosen at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The story spreads; the county reopens the eviction cases. Silas's family gets a stay. Beatrix loses the scholarship and gains something stranger: the committee's youngest member offers her a paid advocacy fellowship for students fighting housing injustice. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: exhausted, uncertain hope.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Graduation day. Beatrix starts a new count — not days remaining, but days begun. She and Silas stand in the parking lot where they were strangers, arguing happily about what comes next. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: release, and a future argued into being.
